title: Cycle Elasticity Blueprint: modular tranches, surge cushion, and release gates
creator: Aisha Chou
description:
Problem: As teams scale Redwood product work, we repeatedly hit mid-cycle capacity crunches that force ad-hoc scope cuts or fire-drill surges. Current guidance is ambiguous about how to price and apply emergency capacity (surge credits), how to split initiatives into modular tranches, and which release gates must be met before shipping. This causes misaligned expectations between PMs, Eng, and Design and reduces predictability for customers and sales.

Proposal: Create a formal "Cycle Elasticity Blueprint" that defines: (1) a modular tranche format for initiatives (core, stretch-1, stretch-2), (2) a limited emergency cushion (surge credit pool) with clear activation triggers and repayment rules, (3) mandatory release gates and quality criteria per tranche, (4) a decision matrix for scope deferral vs. staffing surge, and (5) tooling changes to surface tranche status in the Roadmap and MRP dashboards.

Outcome: Provide product and eng leads a repeatable process to make transparent trade-offs mid-cycle with minimal disruption to velocity and customer-facing commitments.
acceptance_criteria: Blueprint doc published in Confluence with examples for 3 canonical initiative shapes (platform infra, API feature, Console UX)
Surge credit policy defined: size, activation owners, approval flow, and repayment mechanism
Tranche schema implemented in Roadmap metadata (tags for core/stretch and release gates visible)
One pilot initiative uses the tranche model during Cycle 2025-W11 and retro completed
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng leads, Design lead, and VP Product
success_metrics: Reduce mid-cycle unplanned scope cuts by 50% in the pilot tranche cluster
Time-to-decision for surge activation <= 24 hours from request to approval
Roadmap accuracy (features delivered vs committed) increases by 15% for initiatives using tranches
Developer sprint churn reduced (fewer reopens from de-scoped work) by 30% on pilot teams
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft blueprint and tranche templates; align with Eng PMs and Design (Aisha leads)
Week 2: Run tabletop sim with Release Ops and Finance to validate surge credit sizing and repayment
risks: If surge credit pool is too small, teams will continue to bypass the process and ship work informally
Administrative overhead could slow down small teams; need threshold rules so only mid+ sized initiatives use it
Mis-specified release gates could create perverse incentives to declare work as 'core' to avoid de-scope
open_decisions: Should surge credit be funded from central product reserves or allocated pro-rata to initiatives? (finance input needed)
What is the formal repayment model for a credit drawdown (future scope reduction vs bill-back)?
Which role has final sign-off for urgent surge activation outside of a weekly cadence? (Ops, VP-Eng, or VP-Product)
